properties.name: LESSONS 2026-09-23: what hxm_program, the first reflow2 hub (a work program over nine NSLS2 repos, 488-node design, 19 decisions in DECISIONS.md), teaches the hub model the dev_reflow2 trial is building, and that reflow2 does not yet hold
properties.source: dev_reflow2 hub session reading sligara7/hxm_program at ff95bd9 (AGENTS.md, DECISIONS.md D-0016/D-0019, IMPROVEMENTS.md I-006/I-007/I-017/I-018, reflow2.json, codegraphs/), against reflow2's live design; Anthony, 2026-09-23: "hxm_program is my first attempt at a hub using reflow2 … We can take any lessons learned and continue to improve reflow2 based on it."
properties.statement:
CONTEXT. hxm_program was the first hub, built BEFORE reflow2 had any hub concept: ONE design for a whole program, holding both program-level content (cross-beamline decisions, requirements, questions) and content about specific member repos (cmp:hextools, cmp:hex-profile-collection, artifacts at paths inside hextools/). The member repos are NSLS2-owned and have no designs of their own, and colleagues who do not run reflow2 read markdown and graphify codegraphs. Five earlier field reports already reached reflow2 (2026-08-05, 08-19, 08-26, 09-10, 09-14). These four lessons were checked against reflow2's design by search on 2026-09-23 and found NOT recorded:

① A HUB'S CHILDREN ARE OFTEN CODE REPOS WITH NO DESIGN, NOT DESIGNS. reflow2 can watch another DESIGN's export (cap:a-declared-dependency-is-watched-not-imported), but a hub over code repos has nothing to watch. hxm_program's own open I-018 ("nothing tells a session that an associated repo moved since the pages last looked", with req:sessions-told-when-associated-repos-move in hxm's design) is this gap, hand-built there as a one-fork watcher. dev_reflow2's hub assumed every child is a reflow2 design; the real first hub shows most are not, at least at first.

② READERS WHO DO NOT RUN reflow2 NEED A FILE-SIDE HOME FOR BINDING CONTENT, AND hxm_program BUILT ONE. D-0016: "only AJ runs reflow2", so every accepted decision, enforced rule and accepted requirement must have a file-side home (DECISIONS.md, AGENTS.md, a page or a planning file), checked by tools/check_repo.py as a ratchet (a baseline that may only shrink), plus an advisory reverse-drift check for file changes a reflow2 session has not seen. reflow2 has no concept of a reader who does not use it. Every consumer with non-reflow2 collaborators (flo2's non-technical users, Alex's colleagues, hxm's beamline staff) will need this, and hxm_program has a working, tested design of it.

③ MOVING CONTENT BETWEEN DESIGNS HAS NO TOOL. Applying the one-home rule (dec:idea-a-fact-has-one-home-across-a-family-of-designs-and-reflow2-enforces-it) to hxm_program means moving repo-specific nodes out of the program design into per-repo child designs. reflow2 can merge designs and mirror surfaces, but cannot MOVE a node set (with its edges, provenance and history) from one design to another, leaving a reference behind. Every hub built the way hxm_program was, one design first and children later, meets this on the day it splits.

④ A HUB MAY BE ABLE TO READ ITS CHILDREN BUT NOT WRITE THEM. dev_reflow2's trial wrote decisions down into reflow2 and flo2 because one person owns both. hxm_program's members are NSLS2 repos maintained by others, where its own I-006 ("no defined way to push changes to the code repos") is open. For such children the hub's "write each decision into the child that owns it" has no permitted target: the write must become a PROPOSAL to the owner (the write-only-at-proposed lean on dec:idea-gap-flows-to-the-dependency), or the child's design must live in a repo the hub owner controls. The hub model needs "read-only child" as a first-class case, not an exception.

ALSO SEEN, NOT A reflow2 GAP: graphify stamps `built_at_commit` from the directory it runs in, not the analysed repo (hxm I-007, open). The hub session asserted the opposite in two records on 2026-09-23 and corrected both after reading I-007. Generated metadata is only as good as its generator, which is the same discipline as rule:success-is-read-from-the-authoritative-object.
